Add a try/except safety net: if the DP construction fails for any n, fall back to a plain floor(sqrt(n)) grid of squares. The construction itself is unchanged, so the scores already at 1.0 should not move.

Add a guard so that large n (above 150) skips the cubic-time DP and uses the plain floor(sqrt(n)) grid padded with zero-side squares. If the DP raises an exception, the same grid is used. The DP construction is unchanged for small n, so the current scores should not move.

Raise the maximum grid size in the DP from 12 to 16 for n ≤ 300, so more grid layouts are searched for mid-size n. For larger n the cap stays at 12 to keep the runtime down. The DP itself is unchanged, so the smaller cases should score the same as before.
Widen the range of grid sizes the DP searches, from isqrt(n)+2 to isqrt(n)+4 (still capped at 12), so that more layouts are considered for small n. The rest of the construction is unchanged.

I reduce the safety shrink on each square's side from 1e-12 to 1e-13 relative. This keeps the layout valid, since float error is about 1e-16, and recovers a negligible amount of side length. The DP construction is unchanged.

I added a second block layout to the DP: two equal j×j blocks in opposite corners of the m×m grid, with the remaining cells filled recursively. The one-block layout is kept and the DP is otherwise unchanged. I have not run this, so I expect it to match or improve the scores but have not confirmed it

I reduce the per-square safety shrink from 1e-12 to 1e-14 relative. Float error is about 1e-16, so layouts should stay valid, and this recovers a tiny amount of side length. The DP is otherwise unchanged.

I reduce the per-square safety shrink from 1e-10 to 1e-12 relative, in both the leaf and the grid emission. Float error is about 1e-16, so layouts should stay valid, and this recovers a small amount of side length. The DP is unchanged, and I have not run this.

I reduce the per-square safety shrink from 1e-10 to 1e-12 relative in both the leaf and grid emission, which recovers a tiny amount of side length. The DP is unchanged, and I have not run this version.

For n ≤ 600, raise the DP's maximum grid size from 10 to 12, so more m×m layouts (with and without a merged j×j block) are searched. The runtime stays small at these sizes, and the time guard on the fixpoint iteration is kept. I have not run this.

I replace the hard-coded 1e-10 safety shrink on each square's side with a single constant of 1e-12, used in the leaf, grid and fallback emission paths. This recovers a tiny amount of side length. The DP is unchanged, and I have not run this version.

I replace the three hard-coded 1e-10 safety shrinks (leaf, grid and large-n fallback) with a single constant EPS = 1e-12. This recovers a tiny amount of side length per square and leaves the DP unchanged. I have not run it.

Replaced the grid baseline with a dynamic program over recursive subdivision. g(t) is the best side-sum for t squares in a unit cell, refined to a fixpoint by max-plus convolutions over m×m grids (m ≤ 10) with an optional merged j×j block. The best splits are then unrolled into explicit squares.
I reduce the per-square safety shrink from 1e-9 to 1e-12 relative, which recovers a small amount of side length per square. The DP is unchanged, and I have not run this version.

I add a second family of layouts to the subdivision DP: two equal j×j merged blocks at opposite corners of an m×m grid (2j ≤ m), with the remaining cells filled recursively. This extends the search space for larger n. I have not run it, so the rebuild and the corner placement are untested.

For n ≤ 300 I raise the maximum grid size in the subdivision DP from 10 to 13, with the cell cap set to MMAX². This lets 11×11 to 13×13 grids with a merged block use all of their cells, and the time guard is kept. I have not run this.

I reduce the per-square safety shrink from 1e-9 to 1e-11 relative, which keeps adjacent squares clear of each other while recovering a little side length per square. The subdivision DP is unchanged, and I have not run this version.
